text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the August 5 edition of Russia's Izvestia newspaper. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government expects that a thousand-fold redenomination of Russian rouble, which will be carried out starting on January 1, 1998, will encourage the "de-dollarisation" of Russia's economy, a top banking official is quoted as saying.
- Russians spent about 20.8 percent of their earnings on buying hard currency, according to official statistics for the last six months.

- The head of Russian Orthodox Church Patriarch Alexiy II is planning to cooperate with President Boris Yeltsin on the amendments to the draft law on religion, strongly criticised for infringing on the rights of non-Orthodox communities.
- American automaker Ford is said to be holding talks on opening a range of joint ventures in Russia.
- Russians won't lose anything, promises the government daily in connection with the redenomination of the rouble from Janaury 1, which was announced on Monday.
- The government has full control over the situation at Svyazinvest holding after selling its shares, says Alfred Kokh, head of the State Privatization Committee.
- Russia's ex-Defence Minister Pavel Grachev expects to get a new job this autumn. The paper publishes Grachev's first interview since his resignation.
- "Sugar fever" has swept Moscow in connection with the rumours that Ukraine was planning to reduce sugar export to Russia. The prices for sugar jumped 15-20 percent.
- Space Mission Control and a programme of Russian Radio are carrying out a joint project to support Russian cosmonauts on the Mir space station by broadcasting their favourite music and songs.
